description: SHRI BODGESHWAR TEMPLE GOA Nestled in the serene surroundings of Mapusa in Bardez Taluka of North Goa district, lies the ancient and revered Bodgeshwar Temple. This temple holds deep historical and cultural significance, attracting devotees from near and far to seek blessings from Kanakeshwar Baba, lovingly known as Bodgeshwar or Bongini by the locals. Let's explore the spiritual allure and festive charm of this sacred abode. SHRI DEV BODGESHWAR TEMPLE HISTORY The origins of Bodgeshwar Temple trace back to ancient times, and it is believed to be associated with the Mandas, a clan of the Jats, who once held a historical empire in the western plateau of Iran around 700 B.C. Over time, the Mandas migrated to India due to internal wars, and some settled in Punjab and Sindh in the sixth and seventh centuries AD. The Bodgeshwar Temple is a living testament to the historical connections of the Mandas in Goa. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE INFORMATION - SPIRITUAL SIGNIFICANCE Bodgeshwar Temple is devoted to Kanakeshwar Baba, revered as 'Angavani,' meaning one to whom vows are made and desires are fulfilled. The temple holds immense spiritual significance for devotees who believe that their prayers will be answered and desires fulfilled by the benevolent Baba. As a result, thousands of devotees flock to this temple, offering prayers and presents as tokens of their devotion. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE MAPUSA FESTIVAL CELEBRATIONS The festival of Kanakeshwar Baba is a grand affair celebrated with great enthusiasm and fervor during the months of December and January at the Shree Dev Bodgeshwar Temple. The annual fair, known as 'Zatra,' is the highlight of the festival, attracting both locals and tourists alike. The bustling fair contributes to the thriving market center of Mapusa, making it an integral part of the region's cultural and social fabric. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE VISITING When planning a visit to the Bodgeshwar Temple, keep the following in mind: - The temple is located about 12 km from Panaji and is easily accessible by road. - Dress modestly and respectfully, as it is a place of worship. - The temple is surrounded by lush greenery, creating a serene ambience conducive to spiritual reflection. - If visiting during the festival, prepare to witness the vibrant celebrations and immerse yourself in the festive spirit. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE Bodgeshwar Temple is a well-known Hindu temple in North Goa, dedicated to Shri Bodgeshwar, who is believed to be a guardian deity. It is a popular place of worship where devotees come to seek blessings and fulfill their wishes. The temple is surrounded by greenery, providing a peaceful atmosphere for prayer and meditation. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE MAPUSA Located in Mapusa, North Goa, Bodgeshwar Temple is one of the most significant religious sites in the area. It is just a few minutes away from the famous Mapusa Market, making it easy for both locals and tourists to visit. The temple is well-maintained and attracts visitors throughout the year, especially during its annual fair. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE HISTORY The history of Bodgeshwar Temple is deeply rooted in local traditions. Shri Bodgeshwar is considered a "Bhutnath" (lord of ghosts and spirits) who fulfills the wishes of his devotees. Many people visit the temple and tie a thread as a symbol of their wish, believing that their prayers will be answered. This long-standing belief has made the temple a sacred and respected place. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE GOA Bodgeshwar Temple is one of the most visited temples in Goa, attracting devotees from all over the state. The temple is known for its unique traditions, serene surroundings, and spiritual significance. Whether you are religious or simply exploring Goa’s culture, visiting Bodgeshwar Temple is a wonderful experience. SHRI BODGESHWAR TEMPLE Shri Bodgeshwar Temple is dedicated to Shri Bodgeshwar, the wish-fulfilling deity. Devotees come here with faith and gratitude, seeking divine blessings for prosperity, protection, and success. The temple is small yet powerful, with a strong spiritual aura that leaves visitors feeling peaceful and blessed. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE JATRA The Bodgeshwar Temple Jatra is one of the most important festivals celebrated at the temple. This annual fair features cultural performances, food stalls, and devotional events. Thousands of devotees participate in the celebrations, making it a grand occasion filled with faith, festivity, and devotion. BODGESHWAR TEMPLE MAPUSA GOA Since it is located in Mapusa, Goa, the temple is easily accessible to locals and tourists. It is well-connected by roads and is close to major landmarks like Mapusa Market and other temples. The temple is an important part of Goa’s cultural and religious landscape, attracting visitors from all walks of life. MAPUSA BODGESHWAR TEMPLE The Mapusa Bodgeshwar Temple is not just a place of worship but also a center of faith and tradition. Many people believe that prayers offered here bring success and remove obstacles. The temple is beautifully lit during festivals, creating a divine and enchanting atmosphere for visitors. It is a great place to experience the local Goan culture. Chapora Fort A historic fort offering breathtaking views of the Arabian Sea and Chapora River. It is famous for being featured in the Bollywood movie Dil Chahta Hai. SIOLIM RIVERSIDE A scenic riverside location where you can enjoy a peaceful walk, spot birds, and relax by the Chapora River. ANJUNA BEACH One of Goa’s most vibrant beaches, known for its beach shacks, flea markets, and nightlife. It is about 20 minutes from Bodgeshwar Temple. VAGATOR BEACH A beautiful beach with red cliffs, scenic views, and a laid-back atmosphere. It is a great place to relax and watch the sunset. BAGA BEACH One of Goa’s most famous beaches, just a short drive from Mapusa, known for its water sports, beach clubs, and lively nightlife. HOW TO REACH BODGESHWAR TEMPLE BY CAR OR TAXI The easiest way to reach Bodgeshwar Temple is by hiring a taxi or driving. It is located in Mapusa, North Goa, and is easily accessible from major locations like Panjim (13 km), Calangute (9 km), and Baga (10 km). BY BIKE OR SCOOTER Renting a bike or scooter is a convenient way to explore Goa. You can ride to the temple using NH66 or internal roads from Calangute, Siolim, or Assagao. Parking is available near the temple. BY BUS Several local buses from Panjim, Calangute, and other parts of Goa stop at Mapusa Bus Stand, which is just 1 km from Bodgeshwar Temple. From there, you can take an auto-rickshaw or walk to the temple. BY TRAIN The nearest railway station is Thivim Railway Station (9 km away). From there, you can take a cab, bus, or rickshaw to reach the temple. Where is Bodgeshwar Temple located?

Bodgeshwar Temple is situated in Mapusa, North Goa, near the Mapusa market.

Who is worshipped at Bodgeshwar Temple?

The temple is dedicated to Lord Bodgeshwar, also known as "Kanakeshwar Baba," a local deity considered the protector of Mapusa.

What is the significance of Bodgeshwar Temple?

The temple is revered as a place where devotees come to fulfil their vows (known as mannats) and seek blessings for protection and prosperity.

When is the best time to visit Bodgeshwar Temple?

The best time to visit is during the annual festival, known as Zatra, which usually takes place in January or February. The temple is beautifully decorated, and the event attracts a large number of devotees.

What are the temple's opening hours?

The temple is open daily from 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM, though hours may vary on festival days.

Is there an entry fee for the temple?

No, there is no entry fee to visit Bodgeshwar Temple; it is open to all.

How can I reach Bodgeshwar Temple?

The temple is easily accessible from Mapusa market by walking or by a short auto-rickshaw ride. Public transport and taxis are also available from other parts of Goa.

Are there any special rituals performed at the temple?

Yes, devotees often make offerings and perform pujas (rituals) to fulfil their vows. The temple priests conduct these rituals daily, and special ceremonies occur during the annual Zatra.
